key_insight: The paper argues that, under a fixed per-query budget, the best way to improve LLM serving quality is to dynamically trade off resampling the current model against rerouting to another model instead of treating them as separate decisions.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a cost-aware policy for deploying LLM routers that can better balance latency, price, and answer correctness in real serving systems.
method: Formulates budget-aware test-time model selection with a per-query cost budget and an imperfect verifier.
Introduces an online resample-or-reroute (RoR) policy that allocates budget by estimated marginal correctness per unit cost.
Grounds the policy in the asymmetry between recoverability from resampling and from routing to another model.
evidence_signal: Replay experiments on regenerated multi-draw correctness tensors from an eleven-model open-weight pool across four benchmarks show RoR achieves a stronger cost-quality Pareto front than several baselines, with the biggest gains on the most heterogeneous benchmark.
watch_item: The gains depend on verifier quality and shrink as the verifier gets worse, so deployment performance may be limited in settings with weak or noisy verification.
paper_title: Resample or Reroute? Budget-Aware Test-Time Model Selection for Large Language Models
